Adjust the sorting rules

Put one email or phone number per line. Use @team.example only if you trust an entire domain. Trusted contacts need an immediate request or a deadline today or tonight. Always-urgent contacts skip that check. These preferences stay in this browser.

Subscription signals always take precedence. “No rush” and “not urgent” keep ordinary trusted messages low priority. Rules use simple phrases, so review the reason and correct mistakes. Saved rule changes re-sort the visible messages without playing alerts.

Priority is not a safety verdict. Urgent wording cannot make an unknown sender trusted. This demo matches the address you enter; it cannot authenticate senders, scan links, or detect every scam. An address that matches your contacts can still be spoofed. Low priority does not mean safe to open.

Demo messages only; no live email or texts. Rules recognize immediate requests, action within an hour, and deadlines today or tonight. They can miss context, so use the explanation on each card and correct mistakes.
